pr_title: drivers/flash: Add flash_get_parameters call to flash API
pr_body:
Provided call returns const pointer to flash_parameters structure that can be used for passing memory parameters from drivers.

Resolves #22063
pr_comments:
**All checks passed.**



*Tip: The bot edits this comment instead of posting a new one, so you can check the comment's history to see earlier messages.*

> 
> 
> I like how code looks like now.
> Is it possible to make `erased_val` configurable for flash simulator via DTS?
> Is it then possible to add test-case with either 0xff and 0x00 erase_value for nvs test (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/tests/subsys/fs/nvs/testcase.yaml)?

Yes. Now the sim flash will have `erase-value` param that allows selection of flash erase value.

> Driver implementation might recognize erase-value in the runtime.

Yeah, but then the value can't be stored in the API structure, which is `const` and the same for all devices used by the specific driver implementation.  In that case we need it to be accessed through a function, not by reading the common structure.
@pabigot ^^understood, right

Maybe the idea of extending the api with a `get_flash_erased_value()` is not the best approach. Maybe it is better/easier to extend the api with a function `flash_iserased(dev, addr, size)` that would do the compare inside the flash driver.

> Maybe it is better/easier to extend the api with a function `flash_iserased(dev, addr, size)` that would do the compare inside the flash driver.

It's true that the motivation for this API change has not been documented as clealy as it could be.

There is a use for initializing a buffer with the intent that any elements not specifically assigned otherwise will not mutate the content of the flash, essentially preserving the unerased parts.  That's currently handled in one situation by first reading the region, modifying parts, and writing the whole thing back.

Is that an approach that would solve #22063 without changing the flash API?

Even in that case knowing the erase value would be necessary to verify that the technique won't break (e.g. flash already has 0xAA instead of 0xFF and user wants to write 0xF3 to set bits 0..3, but the result would be 0xA2 which has the wrong value in bits 0..3).

@pabigot, I think this case is different, nvs is searching for the end of the fs by searching for a unwritten value. The read and rewrite to update the flash data will not help.
@pabigot, regarding the read and rewrite for mcuboot support, it might be a bad idea to support this in general, the result might be that flash wear is a lot faster than expected or the method is not supported at all by the hardware. Mcuboot afaik always states that they do not need byte access write, if mcuboot does need read and write back it would be best to add this in mcuboot.

@Laczen @nvlsianpu @pabigot I have search for information on flash and eeproms to find if there is device that does erase to non-1 value but I have failed to identify any. 
There are FRAM (FeRAM) devices and MRAM, but they behave like RAM generally which means that they do not require erase prior to write.

Maybe this PR should be dropped. I can not find an example of non-1 erase value.

OK, so NVS would not work with some other erase values: yes but we do not have example of such.
In case of FRAM and MRAM (which are also non volatile), the NVS will not work on them either because they do not have "erase value". Support for them  could be emulated via flash API if we add erase functions for them that would default the RAM to all 1 (which will cost us some time). Note that some FRAM/MRAM may have Lock/Unlock or write features as does EEPROM.

Of course I have forgotten about  SRAM,DRAM battery backed things that basically FRAM and MRAM behave like. Those also does not have erase value and but may be "formatted" to have one at startup and then have erase emulated to write whatever we want them to erase to. But again this is waste of cycles.

EDIT: 2020-06-10
I have mentioned flash and EEPROM memories as one thing, but  EEPROM memories that can write bytes or pages also do not require erase (e.g. AT24CM02), although they may support it as feature e.g.  EEPROM 25AA512 that does not require erase prior to write but provides such feature.

> Mcuboot afaik always states that they do not need byte access write, if mcuboot does need read and write back it would be best to add this in mcuboot.

Mcuboot doesn't and won't use any read-modify-write to flash. It just need to know what the erased value is for working properly on SoC of 0x00 and 0xFF erased values

@de-nordic +1 for introducing this API.
cc @utzig

>

@nvlsianpu  I still voice my concern regarding other technologies of NV type memories, but I am modifying the PR to implement @pabigot suggestions regarding the callback instead of data member.  Additionally I will change it from erase specific callback to `flash_get_capabilities`, `flash_get_params` or similar, that could be used in more general way to obtain flash parameters that could be defined during compilation or run-time.

I am also looking into NVS driver to figure out how would it be possible to make it work with non-volatile memories that does not require erase prior to write.
@pabigot can you re-review please?
Maybe for memories which have not defined erase-value (or erase is not an operation for them) API can return -ENOSUP etc.

> 
> 
> @pabigot can you re-review please?

There are no changes yet. I am still working o it. @pabigot I will let you know when I will have something to present, although I would like to hear your point of view on current support of NV type memories in Zephyr and whether flash/eeprom api shouldn't be merged under one NV API that would also cover capabilities of other type of NV memories.
Actually I would also encourage @nvlsianpu  and @Laczen, to voice their opinions on the subject as they are more experienced, than me, with the Zephyr API and NV memory usage within the system.
Thanks in advance!

> I would like to hear your point of view on current support of NV type memories in Zephyr and whether flash/eeprom api shouldn't be merged under one NV API that would also cover capabilities of other type of NV memories.

I think it's something to consider but @henrikbrixandersen initiated that API and should weigh in on whether its operations can be supported with the flash API.  I assume in that situation we'd need to define the expected behavior of erase: should it do nothing, or should it write a constant to remove any information present (I would propose the latter).

I support moving to `flash_get_parameters` to retrieve information about the flash including erase value.  It should be passed a pointer to a `struct flash_parameters` so we can extend what we can retrieve without adding API.

I say `parameters` above because there's also Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters in #25851, so "parameters" to describe common attributes of the devices makes some sense.  I do **not** believe that the API being discussed here should accommodate the functionality being added in #25851.
`flash_get_parameters` sound good to me as well.

Side note: Cypress PSOC-062 seems to erase flash to 0 (12.5.6   Erase All, [tech ref pdf](https://www.cypress.com/documentation/technical-reference-manuals/psoc-6-mcu-psoc-62-architecture-technical-reference-manual))

> I think it's something to consider but @henrikbrixandersen initiated that API and should weigh in on whether its operations can be supported with the flash API. I assume in that situation we'd need to define the expected behavior of erase: should it do nothing, or should it write a constant to remove any information present (I would propose the latter).

We had the discussion of whether to use the flash API for EEPROM devices (and whether to add an erase API function) back when the EEPROM API was introduced. Please see #19972 for details.

@de-nordic, it seems that the flash api extension is getting defined.

IMO the best way to use this extension in nvs is to extend the nvs fs structure with a pointer to the flash parameters and to set this during nvs_init. If any of the required flash parameters is missing raise a cfg error and keep the nvs flash_device = null. In the nvs routines use the nvs pointer to flash parameters  (so the get_flash_param() is only used in nvs_init and not inside any other nvs routines).

Yes, `const` qualifier 'protects' here the structure as it is in the part that declares pointed type. If you want to protect pointer, you need to move `const`:
`struct *const flash_parameters`
or you can have both:
`const struct *const flash_parameters`

issue_context.title: fs/NVS: NVS is not compatible with flash memories which have 0x00 as erased
issue_context.body:
**This is informative issue**, not a bu really
NVS design assumes 0xff as memory erased state. So it will doesn't work on devices which has 0x00 as erased byte state (e.g. some stm32 embedded. ~~and native_posix with the flash simulator~~ )

**To Reproduce**
~~Try NVS sample using native_posix target~~
[EDIT]: native_posix was fixed
Try NVS sample using a target which have 0x00 as erased byte flash value.
comments: In general it would be good (and trivial) to add support in nvs for devices that use 0x00 as erase value. This however would not solve the problem with flash simulation on native posix. In the flash simulator on native posix the flash area is filled with 0x00 at start but is set to 0xff after erase. For the flash simulator on native posix it would be better to erase (set to 0xff) on creation of flash.bin.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/22089 makes native_posix flash driver compatible with NVS.

The solution https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/25947 does not seem to fix the problem entirely. The https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/22be0d8fd5902da11c9bf55a44012abc7c2cf1c1 has been applied to disable NVS test temporarily.

@de-nordic After check, only L0/L1 use 0x00 as erase value (I guess reason is they have an EEPROM and this is easier to use same erase value for both).
Since L0/L1 have no flash driver yet, proposed code is fine. Maybe adding a warning comment in case of L0/L1 future addition would be a nice thing though.
@erwango Thanks for the information. Will add warning information.

There is a PR for an L0 driver (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/25245) that will hit this issue. The easiest way to distinguish between the EEPROM and FLASH implementations is probably to check for the FLASH_CR_LOCK (erase value 0xff) or FLASH_PECR_PELOCK (erase value 0x00). It's not exactly pretty, but it avoids hard-coding the SOC family.
